pageCache.text:
Headteachers Welcome
Welcome to Days Lane Primary School
Welcome to Days Lane Primary School. We hope our website gives you a clear insight into daily life at our school and the strong sense of community we are proud to share.
Our school values — Resilience, Respect, Responsibility, Compassion, Community and Excellence — underpin everything we do at Days Lane. They guide our approach to learning and behaviour and help children develop the skills and attitudes they need to flourish. Every child is known as an individual, and strong partnerships with parents and carers are central to our work, ensuring all children feel safe, supported and inspired to achieve their very best.
Our dedicated pastoral team and SENCO work closely with children and families to promote inclusion, positive mental health and wellbeing. We are committed to nurturing the whole child and providing targeted support whenever needed.
We aim to develop curiosity and a genuine love of learning. Our engaging curriculum encourages children to embrace new challenges with confidence, becoming independent, resilient and creative learners. We have high expectations for both learning and behaviour, and our children take pride in meeting them.
Learning at Days Lane extends well beyond the classroom. Our spacious grounds provide excellent opportunities for outdoor learning, sport and enrichment. We offer a wide range of clubs and extra-curricular activities, including music, drama, coding and a variety of sports.
Our facilities include:
Nursery – a warm, welcoming and stimulating environment where our youngest children are nurtured through play-based learning. Our experienced early years team work closely with Reception staff to ensure a smooth, confident and happy transition into school life.
Forest School area – supporting outdoor learning and enhancing our Early Years Foundation Stage provision
Music provision – specialist music teachers, keyboard and violin lessons, choir and performance opportunities
Large playing fields – supporting a strong programme of sport, competitions and physical activity
One-to-one Chromebooks in Key Stage 2 – enabling children to develop digital skills, enhance learning across the curriculum and prepare for the next stage of their education
After-school clubs – led by school staff, coaches and specialist providers to further enrich children’s experiences
Wraparound care – on-site provision for pupils from Reception to Year 6, staffed by familiar school adults and offering a range of engaging activities
We celebrate both effort and achievement, believing that enjoyment, positive mental health and wellbeing are essential for children to thrive. Our aim is for every child to develop the skills, confidence and attitudes needed to contribute positively to the wider community and to become a lifelong learner.
We would be delighted to welcome you to Days Lane Primary School and show you our wonderful school in person.

pageCache.pageTitle: Days Lane Primary School - Core Values
pageCache.text:
Core Values
At Days Lane we pride ourselves on our core values of Resilience, Responsibility, Respect, Community, Compassion and Excellence. These values are part of every aspect of school life and take the place of traditional school ‘rules’.
We use our core values to spot and celebrate when children make good choices and to support and encourage them when they make mistakes; helping them to reflect on and think about how they might act differently in the future.
Children at Days Lane will soon become familiar with our child friendly core value characters, which include large puppets of each character, children’s own core values pupil booklet (from Year 1) and a core values parent booklet. Alongside these resources, we have core values stickers and certificates that relate to each value and are awarded to children for demonstrating the values.
Inside the parent booklet you will find a child friendly story to explain what each character represents, including their choice of clothing and accessories.
The pupil booklet unpicks the characteristics of each value in child friendly language and is updated termly by teachers, who discuss them regularly to develop children’s understanding of how they can demonstrate the values through their choice of words and actions. The pupil booklets are kept in school and have been designed to move up with each child as they move through the school. It also includes a space for self-reflection at the end of each academic year.
Nursery and Reception parents – please note that children are introduced to the characters through the puppets and are awarded stickers and certificates in Nursery and Reception. The pupil booklet will be started when children enter Year 1.
We very much hope that you will talk to and promote our core values at home and celebrate when your child is given a core values sticker or certificate and ask them what they did to receive it.
We want our pupils to develop into well-rounded young citizens both inside and outside school and our core values are key to helping achieve this in partnership with parents.
Reggie Responsibility
Colin & Cara Compassion

Our Values, Vision and Ethos
Our Values, Vision and Ethos
Our Core Values
At Days Lane we pride ourselves on our core values of Resilience, Responsibility, Respect, Community, Compassion and Excellence. These values are part of every aspect of school life and take the place of traditional school ‘rules’.
Our Days Lane Core Values form the basis of the way pupils and staff engage with each other; they provide guidance for pupils and staff when responding to a range of situations, and they underpin the key learning habits of successful learners.
At Days Lane Primary School we provide a foundation for life in a happy, high achieving school, where all individuals have high expectations of themselves, respect each other and strive to excel. The school offers a wide range of learning experiences based on a progressive and exciting curriculum, which we continually evaluate and develop.
We believe passionately in providing a blend of academic challenge, moral development and enrichment that allows for the holistic development of each pupil in our care and recognise the importance of every child as a unique individual, each with their own gifts and talents.
It is our aim to build a successful partnership with parents so that pupils are given every possible opportunity to flourish. We nurture good behaviour through building relationships with pupils and engaging them in exciting learning experiences.
The whole school community - children, staff, parents and trustees are proud to belong to the school and hope that pupils and their parents will regard the years spent at Days Lane to be enjoyable, valuable, purposeful and productive.

The children's design brief was to make a moving mascot for a character in the text 'The Firework-Maker's Daughter. The children learnt about pneumatic systems and applied their knowledge to make their product and then evaluated it.

Year 6 children carried out market research in Year 2 and then designed and constructed a moving rainforest toy, using their knowledge of cams, levers and other mechanisms. The children's knowledge of the topic was then assessed through an end of topic quiz.

Year 1 Hanging Decorations:
Year 1 children's design brief was to make a hanging decoration. They explored and evaluated existing products, made their own designs and learnt how to use running and cross stitches to join materials together. They the evaluated their product against their design brief.

Year 5 Seasonal Pies
Year 5's product brief was to design and make a savoury autumn pie. During their learning journey, they learnt all about seasonality, tasted different foods and spices to investigate the effect of combining ingredients and also learnt about the different nutrients and substances within a range of foods. They then used this knowledge to select their ingredients and developed their cooking techniques when making their pie, before finally evaluating their final product.

PSHE
Personal, Social and Health Education (PSHE)
We are proud to be a part of the myHappymind Family! We believe that a child’s understanding of themselves and the world in which they live is fundamental. At Days Lane, Personal Social and Health Education is taught weekly using myHappymind+, a comprehensive, online scheme of work. It is an NHS-backed curriculum and a whole school programme grounded in science and dedicated to building positive mental wellbeing. myHappymind helps children understand how their brains work and creates a culture that helps to build children's resilience, confidence, and self-esteem. myHappymind also teaches the children how to self-regulate and manage their emotions in stressful times, allowing them to be their very best selves! Learn more here:
https://myhappymind.org/
Every year group from Early Years to Year 6 has a separate version of the curriculum, with Year 6 focussing on transition. The curriculum contains quizzes, songs, animations and more and features consistent characters that the children get to know and recognise. The content is structured against the five modules shown below. Each Year group works through the 5 modules allowing for a whole school culture to build.
The myHappymind curriculum is grounded in scientific research and helps children to:
Meet Your Brain - Understanding how your brain works and how to ensure we look after it so that we can manage our emotions and be at our best. Growth mindset is a key part of this too.
Celebrate - Understanding your unique Character Strengths and learning to celebrate them. This is a fantastic module for building self-esteem.
Appreciate - Understanding why gratitude matters and how you can develop gratitude as a habit. Gratitude is key to well-being and resilience and we're all about making it a lifelong strategy!
Relate - Understanding why positive relationships matter and how to build them. We're focussed on the building blocks of good relationships and friendships.
Engage - Understanding how to set meaningful goals that matter and how to stay resilient in times of challenge. This module is all about building self-esteem and resilience too.
The myHappymind programme encourages you to carry on the learning at home too. You can download the Parent App to learn all about the Science of Happiness and also access a range of games, songs, Happy Breathing resources and much more at home. Click on the link to take a look!
https://myhappymind.lpages.co/myhappymind-parent-app-introduction/

Phonics
Curriculum Subjects
Phonics at Days Lane Primary School
At Days Lane Primary School, we believe that learning to read is one of the most important skills a child will develop. We want every child to become a confident, fluent reader, who enjoys books and reading for pleasure. To support this, we follow the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised systematic synthetic phonics (SSP) programme from Nursery through to Key Stage 1.
Little Wandle SSP teaches children to read and spell by explicitly linking sounds (phonemes) to letters or groups of letters (graphemes). Children learn how to blend sounds to read words and segment words to spell, with lessons taught daily in a clear, structured and consistent way. Reading books are closely matched to the sounds children are learning, ensuring success and confidence from the very start.
Phonics learning is carefully sequenced and builds gradually as children move through the school.
In Nursery, children focus on developing their listening skills. This phase lays the foundations for phonics by helping children to tune into sounds in the environment and in spoken language.
Phase 1 does not involve letter learning but is vital in preparing children for reading and writing.
Children begin learning letters and their sounds. They are taught to blend sounds together to read simple words and segment words to spell.
Children are taught more complex sounds, including digraphs (two letters making one sound).
This phase consolidates learning and focuses on reading and spelling words with adjacent consonants (e.g. lamp, frog, desk).
No new sounds are introduced in Phase 4.
In Phase 5, children learn that some sounds can be spelled in more than one way and that some letters can make different sounds.
By the end of Phase 5, children are well prepared for the Year 1 Phonics Screening Check and to move confidently into independent reading and spelling in Key Stage 2.
Parents play a vital role in supporting phonics and reading. We encourage children to read their fully decodable Little Wandle reading books for 10 minutes daily at home and to practise saying the sounds correctly. We provide workshops, guidance and resources to help you understand how phonics is taught and how best to support your child’s reading journey.
By working together, we aim to give every child the strongest possible start in reading and writing.
